segments.title: 第86章 顏竹笙的發現
segments.content:
Reigniting the Verdant Years, Chapter 86: Yan Zhusheng's Discovery

"Alone I stand in the autumn cold."

"The Xiang River flowing north."

"On the tip of Orange Isle."

"Do you remember?"

"Striking the water midstream,"

"The waves stopping the speeding boats?"

"Mmm, Class Monitor, you passed." Zhu Huiyan, who sat at the desk in front, pushed up her round glasses and put a checkmark next to Li Luo's name on the form.

Zhu Huiyan sat in front of Li Luo and was Class 8's Chinese literature representative. For any texts studied in Chinese class that required memorization, students had to pass a recitation test with the class representative within a week.

"I don't think I've ever seen you memorize texts at school," Yan Zhusheng glanced at him. "You're always reading other books during morning self-study."

"That's because I've already finished the Chinese textbook," Li Luo瞥了眼同桌，隨后說道，"I've already memorized everything that needs to be memorized."

"You've memorized the ones we haven't learned yet, too?"

"Of course." Li Luo nodded and looked at Zhu Huiyan in the front row. "I might as well recite the next few texts right now."

Because the mid-term exams were scheduled not long after the National Day holiday, the Chinese curriculum wasn't taught strictly according to the table of contents. Instead, all the texts that required memorization in the first semester of tenth grade were taught first, followed by the others.

So in last week's four Chinese classes, they had already learned three poems.

These included "Snow—to the tune of Qinyuanchun," "A Short Song," and "Returning to Live in the Country."

But just as Li Luo was about to tackle all three texts in one go, the bell for morning self-study rang.

Since it was a Monday, the "March of the Athletes" began to play. It was time for each class to line up and go downstairs for the Monday flag-raising ceremony.

This was the first time the tenth-grade students had participated in the No. 1 Affiliated High School's flag-raising ceremony.

This time, however, Li Luo found something quite similar to his past high school life.

Everyone lined up to gather in the center of the sports field, baking under the hot sun. After the flag-raising was complete, they listened to the principal's speech from the stage, followed by the dean of students, and then the student representative.

Li Luo was originally lost in his own world, standing in line but with his mind in his memory palace, playing the Ultraman Tiga series he had downloaded out of boredom, believing in the light under the scorching sun.

Then he saw Ying Chanxi go up on stage to speak as the tenth-grade student representative.

Well, isn't this great.

It was like this in middle school, and nothing has changed in high school.

Li Luo could always see his outstanding childhood friend shining brightly on stage at public events.

But this time, Ying Chanxi wasn't the only one shining.

After she finished her speech and left the stage, Xu Youyu went up as the eleventh-grade student representative.

Li Luo watched, sighing inwardly. Living under the same roof with these two monsters was truly immense pressure.

If it weren't for his rebirth and the memory palace, he would have developed a serious inferiority complex.

Thinking this way, Li Luo could almost understand his past self a little better.

Back then, facing Ying Chanxi, he really was so insecure he became overly sensitive.

When he had just been reborn, his 35-year-old self no longer cared much about school grades. He could view a god-tier student like Ying Chanxi with a calm and indifferent heart.

But now, as he gradually re-experienced high school life, the reality of it started to sink in again, and Li Luo realized just how ridiculously amazing Ying Chanxi was.

And aside from Ying Chanxi, there was another ridiculously amazing person, Xu Youyu.

If Ying Chanxi were just good at studying, that would be one thing. Even if she ranked first in the grade for every single subject, which was already heaven-defying, at least it was all confined to academics.

But Xu Youyu not only maintained her first-place ranking, held positions in the student council and literature club, but was also writing a web novel at the same time.

Although *The Age of Arts* was performing only moderately right now, with just over a thousand average subscriptions.

In Li Luo's memory, this book would break into the "Boutique" category in its second year, and by the time it was nearly finished in its third year, it would smoothly surpass ten thousand subscriptions.

If it weren't for the fact that Qidian's Twelve Heavenly Kings award at that time required books to have started serialization that same year, Xu Youyu would have definitely become a Heavenly King with that one book.

And she was only in her final year of high school at that time.

She was truly balancing her studies and a part-time job perfectly.

One had to remember, the *Age of Arts* she was writing wasn't a formulaic, entry-level novel like Li Luo's *I'm Really Not a Star*. It was content that leaned more towards the literary and plot-driven side.

To write something like that, she must have regularly read all sorts of miscellaneous books and watched many movies and TV shows from that era.

He had no idea how she did it.

A true master of time management.

While Li Luo was sighing to himself, the twelfth-grade student representative also went on stage.

It was a tall and handsome boy named Xue Yongbin, who was likely the top student of the twelfth grade.

After finishing his speech, Xue Yongbin didn't step down. Instead, still holding the microphone, he continued to speak as the student council president, announcing a series of trivial matters like last week's "Civilized Class" awards.

After standing on the sports field for about twenty minutes, the flag-raising ceremony finally concluded.

As they filed back into the air-conditioned classroom, everyone let out a sigh of comfort, feeling like they had been brought back to life.

Zhu Yufei walked back to his seat. He had already confirmed that Teacher Kong had gone upstairs before entering the classroom. So, taking advantage of the few minutes left in the morning self-study session, he secretly pulled his phone out of his desk drawer.

"Last week's update was a Shuraba scene, it was so damn exciting," Zhu Yufei whispered to Zhang Guohuang.

"I read it." Zhang Guohuang nodded with a grin. "This damn author is so good at writing. He completely has the two female leads wrapped around his finger and managed to bluff his way through it."

"Hmm? Where are you reading this from?" Zhang Guohuang leaned over for a look, then said in surprise, "Why does this cost money?"

"This is the official version," Zhu Yufei said. "I saw people in the QQ group saying the author released 'Annual Rings' on music platforms, so I got curious and checked out that day's chapter."

"But I couldn't see the author's notes on the pirate site, so I subscribed to the official version."

"Look, you can see what the author said here."

Zhang Guohuang blinked, looking somewhat lost. "Aren't web novels all free to read? Why are some paid?"

"You don't know?" Zhu Yufei was even more surprised than him. "The free ones are all pirated. I thought you knew. Otherwise, how would the authors make money? We even have to pay for our school textbooks."

"I never really thought about it that much," Zhang Guohuang scratched his head. He had never really looked into it before. "So are you planning to read on the official site from now on?"

"No way." Zhu Yufei shook his head repeatedly. "How much pocket money do I have? I was just curious enough to subscribe to one chapter to see what the author said. It's only ten cents a chapter, so it doesn't hurt."

"True," Zhang Guohuang nodded in agreement, then asked curiously, "So, is that song 'Annual Rings' any good? I finished the book over the weekend and didn't even know there was a song."

"It's pretty good, this author's got some skills," Zhu Yufei chuckled. "I'll let you listen to it in the dorm tonight."

As the two were talking, a hand suddenly shot out from between them and snatched Zhu Yufei's phone.

The grab nearly scared the soul out of Zhu Yufei. Before he even turned his head, the words had already left his lips: "Teacher Kong, I was wrong... er... wait... Class Monitor, you scared me to death!"

"Oh, I was just curious." Li Luo glanced at the reading page and was pleased to see it was indeed the official Qidian reading app. "Weren't you reading on that -ge site? Why are you reading the official version now?"

"I only subscribed to this one chapter to see what the author said." Zhu Yufei quickly took his phone back. "Don't accidentally click anything, I'll lose money if you subscribe to more."

Li Luo: "..."

Damn it, and here I thought the kid had seen the light.

Li Luo, who had just returned from the restroom, his face darkening, sat back down at his desk speechlessly.

Just then, Yan Zhusheng turned to look at him and asked curiously, "What are they looking at?"

"Nothing, just a web novel," Li Luo waved his hand, signaling for Yan Zhusheng not to probe further.

But Yan Zhusheng frowned and said, "But I thought I heard them mention 'Annual Rings.' Isn't that your song?"

At these words, a cold sweat broke out on Li Luo's back. He quickly tried to soothe and redirect her, "They probably just happened to hear it. They were all saying how well it was sung."

"Oh, I see." Yan Zhusheng nodded, not thinking much of it.

But when evening self-study ended that night, she followed the crowd back to the dormitory, took a quick shower, and lay down on her bed. She then pulled out her phone and logged into QQ Music.

With Li Luo's words "they were all saying how well it was sung" in her mind, Yan Zhusheng put on her headphones. As "Annual Rings" began to play, she tapped open the song's comment section, wanting to see what kind of praise it was getting.

But after entering the comment section, the expression on Yan Zhusheng's face froze.

Here because of the hype

*I'm Really Not a Star* tour group, checking in!

Brother Ran is amazing, he actually came out with a song

Why is it a girl's voice? Is Chong Ran a girl?

Didn't you see the author's note? He asked a friend to help him sing it

Damn, you can tell she's a beauty just from her voice. The damn author deserves to die! How can this be a 'platonic' friend?

Is this guy writing an autobiography? His lovey-dovey life with three female celebrities? Is this 'Sheng Sheng Bu Xi' one of them?

If this is an autobiography, I'll eat my computer right now

It's probably just the damn author's deathbed fantasy. Maybe he has a secret crush on this friend who's singing? Look at this sad love song he wrote, it's a textbook case of unrequited love.

Looking at the comment section, which had a completely different vibe from what she had imagined, Yan Zhusheng was lost in thought for a moment.

What kind of book is *I'm Really Not a Star*?

These people are calling Li Luo "damn author"... so Li Luo wrote this book?

But what does the book have to do with the song?

Yan Zhusheng was utterly baffled, wondering if she should call Li Luo and ask.

But at that moment, Zhu Huiyan, who was also in the dorm, suddenly started talking about Li Luo: "I feel like the Class Monitor's memory is absurdly good. He came to me to recite the two poems we just learned today right after class."

With someone starting a topic, and about the class monitor Li Luo no less, the other girls quickly joined in.

"Didn't we figure that out at the start of the semester? You're only realizing it now?"

"When we were nominating a physics class representative, he directly named the three people who scored above 170 on the science portion of the high school entrance exam. I was stunned. He can even remember something like that for so long."

"Then you guys better be careful. Don't tell him the color of your underwear, or Li Luo will remember it for a lifetime."

"Hahahaha, you're so mean. You're probably the only one who would say that."

Hearing this, Yan Zhusheng immediately gave up the idea of calling Li Luo on the spot. Instead, she searched for the book *I'm Really Not a Star*.

And then, she discovered that she seemed to have opened the door to a whole new world.

(End of Chapter)
